name: Focus and window raise
plain: Can move focus between elements; cannot pull the window to the front or steal focus from other apps.
meaning: A page can focus its own elements, but browsers stop it from grabbing focus from the address bar, another tab or another app, which blocks keystroke capture and pop-over scams.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes cannot call focus() on parent or take focus without activation (Chrome 64)
steps: Browser moves focus only inside the page or when the window is already active

limits.headline: Can move the cursor between boxes on its page, but can't pull its window forward
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you use the page, or when it finishes loading.
can: Move the typing cursor to a form box on its own page
Bring its own tab back into focus after you click on it
Highlight a button or field after you finish a step
cannot: Pull its browser window above your other apps
Steal typing from another app or another site
Jump to the front when you are in a different tab
Force a tab to open in front of the one you are in

story.what_it_is: A page can move the typing cursor between its own fields but cannot yank your whole window forward.
story.for_you: A search box can be ready to type the moment a page opens. A site cannot pull itself in front of the game or document you are using in another app.
story.for_makers: Makers use autofocus to save you a click on login and search forms. Browsers block pushing the window to the front to prevent pop under annoyances.

use_cases.example: A store's search bar is ready for typing the moment the page loads.
A browser game grabs keyboard focus on load so arrow keys work without a click.
A chat app puts the cursor in the message box after you open a conversation.
Old pop under ad tricks tried to pull a window forward, which browsers now block.
A dialog moves focus into itself and back out so keyboard and screen reader users do not get lost.
A login page puts the cursor straight into the username field.

technical_bounds: window.focus() is a no-op in modern browsers unless the person triggered it (Chrome, Safari) or dom.disable_window_flip=true (Firefox default)
Background tabs cannot raise themselves; notification clicks can focus the client via clients.focus (needs a click)
Cross-origin iframe focus() without user activation is blocked (Chrome 64)
Cannot read keystrokes outside the document or in the browser UI
autofocus on a page that is not visible does nothing

history.change: Cross-origin iframes need user activation to move focus
